title: NSS Feed Output Format: Session Logs

blocks.text: The Session Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) feed specifies the data from the Session logs that the NSS sends to the security information and event management (SIEM) system. You can configure an NSS feed by including one or more fields. The fields and their values display in the NSS feed output.
The following tables display information about the Session fields and possible values for those fields.

table: The log time (i.e., when the NSS logs a transaction)
The time and date of the transaction. This excludes the time zone.
The time zone. This is the same as the time zone you specified when you configured the NSS feed.
Client source IPv4 address. For aggregated sessions, this is the client source IP address of the last session in the aggregate.
Client source port. For aggregated sessions, this is the client source port of the last session in the aggregate.
Client destination IPv4 address. For aggregated sessions, this is the client destination IP address of the last session in the aggregate.
Client destination port. For aggregated sessions, this is the client destination port of the last session in the aggregate.
Traffic forwarding method used to send the traffic to the firewall
Zscaler Client Connector tunnel name used to send the traffic to the firewall
Server destination port. For aggregated sessions, this is the server destination port of the last session in the aggregate.
Server destination IPv4 address. For aggregated sessions, this is the server destination IP address of the last session in the aggregate.
Server source IPv4 address. For aggregated sessions, this is the server source IP address of the last session in the aggregate.
Server source port. For aggregated sessions, this is the server source port of the last session in the aggregate.
Abbreviated code of the country of the server IP address
Number of sessions that were aggregated
Name of redirect rule that was applied to the transaction
Cloud Connector or Branch Connector self-rule name that was applied to the transaction
Obfuscated Cloud Connector or Branch Connector self rule name
Number of bytes sent from the server to the client
Number of bytes sent from the client to the server
The network service that was used
Cloud Connector or Branch Connector name
Cloud Connector or Branch Connector virtual machine (VM) name
Cloud Connector or Branch Connector group name
Cloud Connector or Branch Connector region name
Cloud Connector or Branch Connector location
Cloud Connector or Branch Connector platform name
Cloud Connector or Branch Connector platform geolocation name (availability zone)
Amazon Web Services (AWS) account ID, Microsoft Azure subscription ID, or Google Cloud Platform (GCP) project ID

blocks.text: A SIEM can have parsing issues whenever a string field has nonprintable or delimiter characters. For that reason, the Zscaler service has URL encoding for fields such as clt_dst_name. There are several other fields that have the same parsing issue, but URL encoding is not suitable. Such fields are encoded using Base64.
Turning on Base64 encoding for all supported fields may result in approximately a 20% drop in performance.
The following fields have been added as Base64 fields:

When the Zscaler service sends logs to the NSS, it hex encodes all nonprintable ASCII characters that are in URLs. Any URL character that is less than or equal to 0x20, or greater than or equal to 0x7F, is encoded as %HH. This ensures that your SIEM can parse the URLs that contain control characters. For example, a \n character in a URL is encoded as %0A, and a space is encoded as %20.
